correctness.rationale: Using the actual 18-edge 11-vertex graph, independently enumerated exactly 123 nonempty faces of Ind(G). An acyclic directed-Hasse matching leaves (one critical 0-cell,two critical 2-cells), proving S^2 vee S^2 rather than merely mod-two homology. Across ALL 23 full/deletion/link complexes, independent enumeration and Kahn topological sorts certify 1465 nonempty face occurrences, 3644 cover incidences and 709 matched pairs, with prescribed local critical counts. Deletions v=3,4 admit 48 free-face collapses each (the source code checks every unique codimension-one coface). All other nine deletions have one 0- and one 2-cell; links at v=3,4 have one 0- and two 1-cells; others one 0- and one 1-cell. The no-1-cell CW models make each 2-cell attaching map constant, giving integral homotopy. The separate adjacency-driven mod-two verifier and spectrum agree. Only this exact labeled graph is proven.

value.rationale: PASS: The Herschel graph is the canonical smallest non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph, providing a mathematically motivated graph-complex benchmark. A COMPLETE integral homotopy profile of all eleven one-vertex deletions and links detects two exceptional collapsible deletions among vertices of equal degree, which neither a graph spectrum nor a homology-only computation captures. The precise local invariant can test new graph-topology reduction and vertex-criticality hypotheses without falsely asserting a general Hamiltonicity theorem.

limitations: Proof is an exhaustive finite theorem for precisely the displayed graph, not a general assertion about polyhedral non-Hamiltonian graphs.
Acyclic matching establishes integral homotopy; mod-two boundary ranks alone would not.
